Investigate compression ratio difference - COMPLETED: Root cause is AVAudioFile's large free box padding (31KB vs afconvert's 3KB), not AAC encoding. Both produce identical mdat (4,588 bytes), decode to identical audio.

Research AVAudioFile free box issue on web - COMPLETED: No viable iOS solution found. ExtAudioFile behaves identically to AVAudioFile (same underlying Core Audio). AVEncoderBitRateKey crashes AVAudioFile. Lower-level AudioConverter C API supports kAudioConverterEncodeBitRate but only affects audio data size (mdat), not metadata padding (free box). AVAudioConverter wrapper doesn't expose bitrate control. M4A transcoding corrupts files. Conclusion: Free box padding (31KB vs afconvert's 3KB) is inherent to AVAudioFile's pre-allocation strategy with no configuration option to reduce it.

Determine time needed for M4A conversion of a large DN10 segment - COMPLETED: AVAudioConverter converts 5.3MB CAF to 280KB M4A in 0.075s (19.15x compression). afconvert: 0.082s → 256KB (20.91x). AVAudioConverter is 8% faster, only 24KB larger file (9% size difference). Performance is acceptable for production use.

name: Replace afconvert CLI with AVAudioConverter in AudioStore

references.text: CRITICAL: AVAudioConverter maintains state - recreating per-buffer causes AAC encoder to prepend 2112 frames of silence

AVAudioConverter produces 37,352 bytes with 31,817 byte free box (85% of file). afconvert produces 8,680 bytes with 3,130 byte free box (36% of file). Identical mdat (4,588 bytes), identical decoded audio.

ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT: Performance data (0.075s conversion time) suggests CAF generation and M4A compaction should be separated. CAF synthesis should complete immediately for fast playback, with M4A compaction deferred to background async task. This avoids playback latency for uncached audio.

SESSION NOTES: AudioStore Sendable analysis. All properties immutable after init: guidStore (@unchecked Sendable), audioType (enum), cc (Sendable with NSLock thread-safety), timeout (TimeInterval). Blocked on T_AZv_4Rvsc: GuidStore has FileManager race conditions in directory creation/deletion that must be fixed before AudioStore can safely be @unchecked Sendable.
ffprobe analysis: both files decode to identical 42KB PCM, both use AAC (LC) codec with skip_samples=2112 priming, identical packet structure
AVAssetWriter (iOS native) has shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse property that places moov atom at beginning of container, optimizing file structure and reducing padding overhead.
ExtAudioFile API behaves identically to AVAudioFile - both use same underlying Core Audio framework. No free box padding control available in either API.
AVEncoderBitRateKey and AVEncoderBitRateStrategyKey cause NSInvalidArgumentException crashes when used with AVAudioFile(forWriting:) settings dictionary.

SESSION NOTES: Deferred M4A conversion architecture implemented. storeAudio caching: check M4A first, then CAF, return M4A if exists else CAF if exists. On cache miss: synthesize to CAF immediately, start Task.detached for background M4A conversion, return CAF URL to caller. Enables playback without waiting for conversion. M4A replaces CAF when conversion completes in background.

SESSION NOTES: Task.detached patterns learned. Use @Sendable on closure to suppress sendability warnings for fire-and-forget background work. Combine with [weak self] capture to prevent keeping AudioStore alive during background M4A conversion. Guard let self before doing work prevents executing if AudioStore deallocated. Error handling via cc.bad1 logs without blocking caller—CAF URL already returned so playback unaffected.
AudioFile size hints (AudioFileCreateWithURL, kAudioFilePropertyEstimatedDuration) control free box allocation but AVAudioFile(forWriting:) wrapper does not expose these parameters
Lower-level AudioFile C API (AudioToolbox) supports AudioFileCreateWithURL with kAudioFilePropertyEstimatedDuration size hints for better pre-allocation control than AVAudioFile wrapper.
Lower-level AudioConverter C API supports kAudioConverterEncodeBitRate property but only affects mdat (audio frame) size, not free box metadata pre-allocation.
AVAudioConverter Swift wrapper does not expose bitrate or encoder properties - no access to underlying AudioConverterRef.
